title: Vinyl Plank in Kitchens: Heavy Appliances, Fridges and Dents
meta: Vinyl plank in kitchens: handling the fridge, range and dishwasher without dents or a trapped appliance, plus the island rule. Wills Flooring, Everett.
keywords: vinyl plank flooring in kitchen, will a refrigerator dent vinyl plank, vinyl plank under appliances, vinyl plank under kitchen island, dishwasher height vinyl plank, vinyl plank installation Everett WA

blocks.lead: Vinyl plank works well in a kitchen with three rules: use a rigid core plank with a 20 mil wear layer, never pin a floating floor under the island or cabinets, and move the fridge on a hardboard runner, never on its wheels. Do that and the appliances will not dent it. Skip it and the fridge leaves four permanent dimples.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs vinyl plank at $2.50 per sq ft for labor with a 500 sq ft minimum. Kitchens are where most of the callbacks in this trade come from, so the details below are the ones we insist on.

blocks.html: The kitchen is where Everett homeowners most want vinyl plank and where it most often gets damaged, and almost none of the damage is from water. It is from a 350-pound refrigerator, a range dragged out for cleaning, and a dishwasher that can no longer come out because the new floor is taller than the old one. Silver Lake kitchens from the 1990s have all three waiting, and Riverside houses add an uneven subfloor.

blocks.text: What actually damages vinyl plank in a kitchen

items.title: Point load, not weight
items.text: A fridge spread over its footprint is fine. The same fridge on four half-inch wheels puts most of its weight on a few square inches, which is how dimples form. Rigid core resists this far better than flexible plank.

items.title: Dragging
items.text: Rolling a fridge or pulling a range straight across the floor scratches the wear layer and can catch a plank edge and lift it. Every appliance move should happen on a hardboard or plywood path.

items.title: Pinned floating floors
items.text: A floating floor has to expand and contract as a sheet. An island or toe kick screwed down through it locks one section, and the seams nearby peak or gap by the first summer. This is the number one kitchen failure we are called to fix.

items.title: Slow leaks, not spills
items.text: Spills wipe up. A fridge water line or dishwasher supply dripping for months finds a seam and soaks the subfloor. A pan under the dishwasher and a braided steel fridge line are cheap insurance.

head: Appliance
The risk
What we do or recommend
rows: Dimples from wheels, scratches from rolling, water line leaks
Move it on a hardboard runner. Set it on wide plastic glides or a fridge mat, not bare wheels. Replace the plastic water line with braided steel.
Scratches from dragging; anti-tip bracket screwed through the floor
Lift or slide on cardboard. Mount the anti-tip bracket to the wall or subfloor through a drilled clearance hole in the plank, never tight to the plank.
New floor is taller, dishwasher cannot come out
Measure the gap before install. Raise the legs, run the plank under it, or stop short and add a filler. Decide before the first plank is cut.
Install the island on the subfloor first, then float the plank up to it with an expansion gap under the toe kick.
Cabinets stay on the subfloor. Plank goes in after cabinets and stops at the kick with a gap covered by shoe molding.
blocks.note: None of this changes the $2.50 per sq ft labor rate. It changes whether the floor still looks right in three years.

blocks.text: The dishwasher trap, step by step

items.text: Old sheet vinyl is about 1/16 inch thick. A rigid core plank with attached pad is 1/4 to 3/8 inch. That difference can trap a dishwasher under the counter lip so it can never be pulled for service.
Most dishwashers have an inch or more of leg adjustment. If the legs can drop enough, we run the plank under the dishwasher so the next unit slides in on a continuous floor.

items.d: Step 3: if the legs cannot drop
items.text: We stop the plank at the front edge of the dishwasher and leave a removable filler strip. Not as pretty, but it beats cutting the countertop to get a dead dishwasher out.

items.d: Step 4: the same check for the range
items.text: A slide-in range has a counter lip too. Confirm it will still slide in and out after the floor rises, and that the anti-tip bracket is reinstalled correctly.

items.html: Silver Lake and Eastmont, 1990s to 2000s. Particleboard underlayment under old sheet vinyl is common. It crumbles when wet and has to come out before plank goes down.
Riverside and Bayside, 1900s to 1920s. Plank subfloors with dips and old fir underneath. Rigid core bridges small dips, but anything over 3/16 inch in 10 feet needs leveling first.
Port Gardner condos. Concrete subfloor, a strict IIC sound rule and a shared elevator for the fridge. Use a plank with a rated acoustic pad and plan appliance day.
Rentals near Boeing. Kitchens turn over hard. A 20 mil wear layer and a mid-tone, varied plank hide the damage between tenants better than anything light and uniform.

blocks.text: When vinyl plank is not the right kitchen floor

a.title: Plank fits when
items: The kitchen flows into a family room and you want one continuous floor
The house has kids, dogs and a dishwasher that has already leaked once
The subfloor is flat or can be leveled affordably
You want a floor that clicks apart for a repair rather than a tear-out

b.title: Choose something else when
items: There is real hardwood next door that you want to match; a hardwood extension ties in better
A commercial-style range or a built-in fridge with a very small footprint is going in; tile takes the load without worry
The slab or crawlspace is damp and nobody wants to fix it first
The kitchen is a high-end Everett remodel where buyers expect wood or tile

blocks.title: The mistake we fix most:
blocks.text: A kitchen floor installed before the cabinets, then the island screwed through it. Perfect on day one. By July the plank has nowhere to expand and the seams next to the island lift. If a contractor floors first for convenience, the island must sit on a plywood block at floor height, not on the plank.

items: Measure dishwasher and range clearance with the new floor thickness added; decide plank-under or filler strip.
Confirm cabinets and island sit on the subfloor, with the plank floated up to them.
Ask what is under the current floor; particleboard has to come out.
Have a hardboard runner and appliance glides on site for the fridge.
Replace plastic water lines with braided steel while the fridge is out.
Get the 1-year workmanship warranty in writing along with the plank's dent and wear warranty.

faq.q: Will a refrigerator dent vinyl plank flooring?
faq.a: Sitting still on wide feet or a fridge mat, no. The dents come from rolling it on small hard wheels or leaving it parked on them. Move the fridge on a hardboard runner and set it on plastic glides. Rigid core plank with a 20 mil wear layer handles a full-size fridge without marks.

faq.q: Should vinyl plank go under the kitchen cabinets and island?
faq.a: Not a floating floor. Cabinets and the island sit on the subfloor and the plank floats up to them with a small expansion gap under the toe kick. Pinning a floating floor under an island causes peaking and gaps within a year. Glue-down plank is the exception, since it does not float.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank go under the dishwasher?
faq.a: Yes if the dishwasher legs can drop enough to clear the counter lip with the thicker floor. If they cannot, we stop the plank at the front and add a removable filler so the unit can still come out. We measure this at the estimate before anything is cut.

faq.q: How much does it cost to put vinyl plank in an Everett kitchen?
faq.a: Installation labor is $2.50 per sq ft with a 500 sq ft minimum, so a kitchen alone is billed at 500 sq ft: 500 × $2.50 = $1,250. Most Everett customers add the adjoining dining or family room to use the minimum. Plank, tear-out, particleboard removal and appliance disconnects are quoted at the free estimate.

faq.q: Is vinyl plank better than tile in a kitchen?
faq.a: It is warmer, quieter, easier on dropped dishes and far easier to repair one plank at a time. Tile handles extreme point loads like a commercial range better and is the expectation in some high-end remodels. For most Everett family kitchens, rigid core plank is the more practical floor.

faq.q: What if a plank does get dented or gouged in the kitchen?
faq.a: Rigid core click plank can be unlocked from the nearest wall or cut out and replaced individually, which is why we always leave you a box of spare planks. A gouge in laminate or a chipped tile is a much harder repair. Keep the spares somewhere dry.
